column2: The reported breadth of the gag orders in State v. Robinson, and the witness-silencing claims attached to them. Where a routine protective order stops being routine is the whole argument.

A reported 600,000-file production landing on the defense while contested raw DNA, ballistics and chain-of-custody data stayed back. Volume and withholding are different complaints, and this page keeps them apart.

Reported claims that basic steps — a gunshot-residue test, bomb dogs, an ambulance on standby — were bypassed at the scene. Critics read the pattern as consistent with something other than a rifle being the story.
Reported claims that the FBI directed the counterterrorism review to stop pursuing leads pointing to a possible foreign nexus. The most consequential thing anyone alleges was stopped.

The exploding-microphone theory as a cover-up item: what is alleged, who alleges it, and what would have to be suppressed for it to be true. The majority citizen reading of the case runs through this page.

Reported claims that volunteer attorneys were turned away while an unrelated inmate was positioned as a possible jailhouse informant. Two separate claims critics read together; each is weak on its own.
Cameras and SD cards reportedly left the scene before investigators catalogued them. If the recordings went with someone, every later frame-level argument is working from a filtered set.

Reported claims that the SUV which carried Charlie to hospital — a primary forensic surface — was scrapped and melted down before any independent testing. If true, the residue question can never be settled.
KUTV and online critics report the Washington County Sheriff's Office returned "no records" for video of the surrender and booking. The footage bears directly on the disputed turn-in time.

The same Trends method applied to two Utah judges — claimed Israeli searches before Charlie's death, none from Utah until after. The method repeats across the case, which is either its strength or its tell.

The Trends screenshots themselves: a claimed December 8-14, 2024 surge for Robinson's lead counsel, geolocated to Israel. See the graph before deciding what a normalized interest index can and cannot show.

The September 2025 ATF report could not tie the autopsy jacket fragment to the seized Mauser. The state is left without an individual physical match between the rifle it names and the object taken from the body.
A .30-06 round carries roughly 3,950 joules against a 9mm's 482. Commentators argue the wound described publicly does not match that energy — the arithmetic is not disputed, the inference is.
The geometry case against a Losee rooftop shot — a 5-to-9 degree downward entry, the C2 path, and the straight-on neck entry claims. Angles are checkable in a way frame-reading is not.
Sealed warrants, gag orders and restricted discovery, and what is scheduled to become public in 2026. A map of the closed doors, which is the precondition for most of the suspicion in this section.
How Robinson's counsel was actually appointed, who represents him, and what public commentary has claimed about the timing. The record version of a question that usually circulates as rumour.
Chest and heart on camera in the first hour, neck in the record afterwards. This page lays the conflicting witness descriptions next to each other rather than choosing between them.

A July 2026 court filing lists injuries far beyond one neck wound — hemopericardium, bilateral hemothorax, brain hemorrhage, lung hematomas, airway cartilage disruptions. The full list is what most arguments here are missing.
A surgeon and a retired cardiologist say publicly that the injuries in the medical examiner's report do not fit a single rifle round fired from the Losee rooftop. Two named clinicians, on the record.

The medical examiner findings quoted in the court filing — hemopericardium, bilateral hemothorax, subarachnoid hemorrhage — scored against two hypotheses side by side. The clearest place to see which mechanism the injuries actually fit.

Two pages of the State's own brief say the bullet travelled downward, then quote the examiner saying it obliterated the left side of C2 through C7. Critics say those statements pull in opposite directions.

Professional four-channel audio recorded about 46 metres from the tent. Researchers say it separates a distant muzzle blast near 120 metres from a louder event at the stage — two events at two locations, if the reading holds.

Witnesses who told cameras within minutes that Charlie was shot in the chest — a description Candace Owens argues never matched the visible neck wound. Why so many people gave the same detail is the open question.
People reached the stage within seconds of the shot, and claims persist that a device left with one of them. If the lavalier transmitter was removed there, the chain of custody breaks at second one.

Project Constitution argues the burnt object in the SUV holds a melted audio jack and a battery-label fragment from the RØDE transmitter. The images, the reasoning and the problems with all of it, set out together.

A self-described former USMC explosive breacher argues a cone of PETN in the crucifix's centre column, anchored by the heavy chain, could fire upward. It is the mic theory's rival, not its ally — both cannot be the mechanism.

What a military high explosive actually is, and why RDX, PETN and TNT-class compounds keep surfacing in this thread. Crucially, what a charge that small would and would not leave behind on fabric and skin.

Frame-by-frame and optical-flow work by independent analysts, including Jon Bray, arguing the movement pattern is omnidirectional rather than along a bullet's path. The imagery is compressed consumer video, which is the standing objection.

The hub for the exploding-mic thread — hardware, audio, AES procurement, SUV fragments and the veteran testimony. Start here if you want the strongest and weakest parts of the theory laid out side by side.
The RØDE Wireless PRO on Kirk's shirt: what the hardware actually is, how it mounts, and how large the transmitter body is. Every device theory on this site has to fit inside those dimensions.

A catalogue of the posts, TV clips and threads claiming Charlie was shot in the heart or chest, set against the absence of any visible chest wound. The pattern is real even when every individual claim is soft.
Lead capital defense counsel in State v. Robinson — Salt Lake City based, thirty years in criminal defense. The person behind the name those Trends screenshots are built on.
The most attributable US intelligence thread on the site: a named official saying his foreign-nexus inquiry was halted. Everything else in that section is softer than this.

The state's own lab could not match the autopsy jacket fragment to the rifle it seized. The defense treats that as exculpatory; examiners would call inconclusive the commonest result in the discipline.
Two sounds, two distances, two locations — roughly 120 metres and roughly 46 metres. If that split holds, the rooftop stops being the only place the harm could have come from.
The routing page for every non-rooftop mechanism — tent shots, the exploding mic, shaped charges, close-range theories. Useful precisely because it shows how many of them are mutually exclusive.
The argument that a rooftop .30-06 cannot match the reported neck wound path, the energy, or the blood evidence. It is the single thread connecting almost every cause-of-death dispute on this site.
Citizen reviewers say roof surveillance shows no muzzle flash and no rifle recoil at the moment Kirk was hit. It is used to argue the roof figure was a decoy rather than the source of the harm.
A five-inch roof lip sits between a prone figure set back from the edge and any view down into the courtyard. The geometry question is simple: what could he actually see?

What citizen investigators have alleged about a named private citizen at the UVU event, recorded with the counterweight attached. No agency has named him a person of interest and no criminal allegation is made here.

The ATF's September 17 lab report reportedly could neither identify nor exclude the Mauser 98 as the source of the recovered jacket fragment. It is the only item in this section resting on a document rather than a thread — and both camps overclaim it.

Proponents zoom into a charred mass photographed in the SUV and read a melted audio jack and a warning symbol into it. The imagery cannot carry that weight, and the theory's own advocates cannot agree which RØDE model it was.

An unnamed analyst says uncompressed Canon XA55 audio holds three low-frequency arrivals, the loudest a detonation at the tent. It is the acoustic backbone of every device theory here — and reflections off campus buildings produce the same pattern.

Recorded as a specimen of what is circulating, not as a claim this site advances. Anonymous accounts read a dark object in a named private citizen's hand as a trigger; he has been charged with nothing and no evidence supports it.

The most-repeated suspicion in the case: a .30-06 carrying roughly 3,950 joules should have blown through the neck and sprayed the tent. The counterargument is strong — and the physics error inside the claim undercuts the analysts making it.

Proponents agree the front neck wound is an exit, then contradict each other completely about where the shot came from — high and behind, or from inside the tent. None has produced medical documentation, and video cannot settle a wound margin.

The RØDE transmitter was reportedly worn under Kirk's shirt, magnetically clasped through the fabric. That one detail is the precondition every contact-device theory needs — and it is also routine professional audio practice.

Both camps treat the snapped silver chain as their clue. One cited expert says cavitation from a bullet snapped it; another says a PETN cone in the pendant did. They cannot both be right, and that is the point.

Twelve numbered suspicions about the official rifle account, ranked honestly — the ATF fragment at the top, the frame-reading at the bottom. Read it to see which alternatives kill each other, because several of them do.

Optical-flow work says the shirt balloons and the chain snaps several frames before any blood appears. It is the strongest of the alternative observations — and hydrostatic cavitation predicts exactly that sequence at 30fps.

The earliest on-camera witnesses described a chest-and-heart wound the white shirt does not show. This thesis says that is the wound the mechanism was meant to produce — and the shirt is also what falsifies it.

Baron Coleman says he is 100 percent convinced Tyler Robinson was framed and is in grave danger of being killed. He offers no evidence of any threat, and Robinson has been held in a high-security unit since September 2025.

Judge Tony Graf entered a publicity order on his own motion, and critics ask why the defense never fought it. Such orders are routine in capital cases and exist mainly to protect the defendant — so the complaint runs against Robinson's own interest.

A transport order moving inmate Jaxson Thomas Fox to a courthouse is read online as a jailhouse snitch being positioned. A transport order is a ministerial docket entry; it reveals nothing about what anyone will testify to.

Daily Mail reporting says officials worried Joe Kent's foreign-interference inquiry could hand Robinson's lawyers a multi-suspect argument. That single quoted sentence is why critics ask what counsel has done to demand the material.

The 6:25 PM Miranda timestamp everyone quotes came out of a defense motion quoting a Bates-stamped exhibit — evidence the defense is working, not failing. Critics still ask why it has not become a public suppression fight.

Washington County refused a news request for the surrender video, then reported it deleted under a 30-day retention policy while pleadings suggest the footage exists. Coleman calls that footage definitive on whether Robinson turned himself in early.

An anonymous post reads a December 2024 Google Trends graph as proof lead counsel was pre-selected from abroad. Trends cannot report IP addresses, and Utah law makes the claim's premise impossible — published here to be examined, not credited.

Nine things citizen investigators flag about Tyler Robinson's legal defense — counsel selection, the unchallenged gag order, the Miranda exhibit, the jailhouse informant. Questions about strategy, not accusations of misconduct against any attorney.

One unsourced list item says Robinson's parents declined high-end attorneys; a second says the prosecutor blocked volunteers. The two claims contradict each other, and a prosecutor cannot choose a defendant's counsel.

Candace Owens argues no sworn written confession exists and points to the not-guilty plea. Critics ask why the defense has not publicly rebutted the confession narrative — though a plea is itself the formal denial.

Candace Owens has claimed the FBI did not want bomb dogs in certain places at UVU, a keystone of the rigged-microphone theory. The investigation file's own record shows bomb dogs were called at 11:17am.

Investigators allege the FBI is reviving Comparative Bullet Lead Analysis, a test the Bureau abandoned in 2005, after the ATF exam came back inconclusive. An attributed inference, not a confirmed fact.

The claim that Robinson's defense sought a continuance because the ATF and FBI would not release files held since September — DNA data, video chain of custody. Attributed and unverified, though it tracks the docket.
Baron Coleman alleges the enhanced stairwell suspect photos went out after Robinson was already in custody and being Mirandized. It is his inference from a Bates-stamped filing, not a finding.

The claim that federal agents told local officers not to talk to witnesses, and that DNA testing on items along the escape route stopped. Attributed and unverified — and it recurs in the cover-up material from a different direction.

Seventeen things citizen investigators flag about the FBI in this case, split into Most Important and Secondary — the halted foreign-nexus probe, the paved crime scene, the seized security-team clothing. Attributed claims, not proven findings.

Per Daily Mail reporting, FBI Director Kash Patel allegedly halted the counterterrorism review of a possible foreign nexus to the killing. Attributed reporting, not a proven finding — and Joe Kent has since spoken on the record.

An unsourced list entry says an FBI Rav4 drove past Tyler Robinson right after the shooting and flashed a badge when pulled over. No source, no date, no agent named — recorded so it can be checked or dropped.

Hands found no gun, dogs found no gun, and the rifle reportedly turned up only after federal agents sent junior local officers back to search again. Unsourced in the file, and squarely relevant to where the rifle was recovered.

TPUSA's October 14 tribute video reportedly used crisp 4K and drone footage from September 10 — footage said elsewhere to be unreleasable on FBI advice. An attributed inference about which version of the day gets shown.
Witness Ryne Simmons says he sent his 4K footage of the shooting to the FBI and was then told to delete his own copy, with follow-up calls. A named witness account, attributed and unverified.
An unsourced list entry says the FBI blocked a surgeon from returning to the room with Charlie Kirk. No name, no hospital record, no source anywhere in the file — kept only so it can be run down.

Two low-confidence optics items: a claim the transport SUV was chopped up and melted down, and a list entry that an FBI building shares a floor with the ADL. Both unverified, and the second proves nothing alone.

Terryl Farnsworth was reportedly filming from a rock pile 27 seconds after the shot and said "He's dead" at 12:24:36. Critics call it foreknowledge; the ordinary reading is a bystander watching a man bleed.

Police audio reportedly carries the first report of the shooting at 12:26, after the SUV had already left with Kirk. Two and a half minutes to a radio channel is fast, not slow — which is why this one deflates on inspection.
A reconstruction places Mikey McCoy phoning his wife at 12:23:30, the same second as the shot. No phone record supports that timestamp; it is an inference drawn from footage.

An unidentified crew reportedly took roughly ten inches of soil out of the tent courtyard before the landscaping contractor arrived on September 14. The ground under the chair is the one surface nobody can re-test.

Every Coleman claim in date order — the custody-versus-Discord argument, the Bates 003996-R2 Miranda reading, the grave-danger clip. Laid out chronologically you can see which claims he built on which.

The reported September 11 surrender at the Washington County Sheriff's Office — the Brooksby timeline, the 6:25 PM Miranda, the missing bodycam, the 33-hour manhunt framing. Everything the surrender video would settle.

Coleman says on the Julian Dorey podcast that Robinson's family does not believe he did it and denies he confessed to them, and notes the parents were absent from the preliminary-hearing witness list.

The argument that a concealed shaped charge fits the wound better than a rooftop rifle shot — the pillar of the case that Tyler Robinson is not the assassin. It stands or falls on the wound, not the roof.
The NCTC director who says on the record that the FBI shut down his Charlie Kirk inquiry before foreign-nexus leads were exhausted. A named official, speaking for himself.

Second-row witnesses describe the impact landing on Kirk's chest and blood coming from the middle of it — one says outright he was shot in the heart. The white shirt shows no chest wound, which is what makes the pattern worth explaining.

The machine behind the audio — what it was, where it stood, and why uncompressed 48kHz capture resolves timing that phone codecs smear together. Read it before trusting or dismissing the acoustic analysis.

Phone and crowd video from September 10 — Ryne Simmons' 4K close-up, Jon Bray's shirt work, Blake Bednarz's recording. Nearly every frame-level argument on this site traces back to one of these files.

Lead counsel Kathryn Nester with Michael Burt, Richard Novak and Staci Visser — appointments, motions and the estimated cost of a capital defense. Living attorneys; nothing here alleges misconduct by any of them.

The FBI and ATF discovery fights — DNA and chain-of-custody materials the defense says were never produced, a reported 600,000-file production, sealed digital forensics. This is where the defense is visibly working.

The December 2025 publicity order, the closed hearings, the March 2026 seal motion over the inconclusive ATF report, and the media coalition that opposed it. Everything the public is not allowed to see, in one place.
The transport order itself, with the process facts separated from the jailhouse-snitch theories built on top of it. Read the document before deciding what it means.
Coleman's case that Robinson turned himself in during the early afternoon of September 11, not after 9 PM — and that Washington County refused or deleted the video that would show it.
If Robinson was in custody with his phone seized at 6:25 PM on September 11, who typed the 7:57 PM Discord message? The whole confession narrative turns on which clock is right.

The inmate whose transport order launched the jailhouse-informant theory, treated here as a post-event narrative figure. A living person charged in an unrelated matter, with no suggestion he intends to say anything untrue.

Where the "arm puller" label came from, and how a TPUSA crew figure in citizen footage became a thread subject. Attributed speculation only; no wrongdoing is alleged against him anywhere on this site.
Kent tells Julian Dorey the National Counterterrorism Center was told to stop investigating potential foreign ties. The interview is the primary source most of the secondhand reporting rests on.
